flawed_step: 0062-0063 (concluding, in the |R_{m-1}| < n/2 case set up at lines 0054-0060, that the padded set S has no neighbor in W_m)
counterexample: Padding introduces neighbors the argument ignores. Concretely, let W_{m-1} contain the unreachable vertex u (u not in R_{m-1}) with an edge u-w for some w in W_m. Nothing in the BFS argument forbids this: R_m = N(R_{m-1}) cap W_m = empty only constrains vertices of R_{m-1}, not the rest of W_{m-1}. If |R_{m-1}| < n/2, the padded S = R_{m-1} cup {u, ...} of size n/2 contains u, so w in N(S) cap W_m, and N(S) is NOT contained in V \ W_m; the bound |N(S)| <= alpha n at line 0067 fails and no contradiction is obtained.
reasoning_summary: Steps 0002-0018 (base case) are sound: if no W1-W2 edge existed, any S subset of W1 with |S| = n/2 (which exists because (1-alpha)n >= n/2, since the hypothesis |N(S)| >= n/2 + alpha n <= n forces alpha <= 1/2) would have N(S) subset of V \ W2, giving |N(S)| <= alpha n < n/2 + alpha n. Steps 0019-0047 (layered BFS, definition R_i = N(R_{i-1}) cap W_i, R_k = empty under the contradiction hypothesis, minimal m with R_m = empty, and the deduction that no vertex of R_{m-1} has a neighbor in W_m) are all correct. The first bullet at 0051-0053 (case |R_{m-1}| >= n/2, take S subset of R_{m-1} of size n/2) is also correct: N(S) subset of N(R_{m-1}) subset of V \ W_m yields the contradiction. The proof fails at the second bullet: when |R_{m-1}| < n/2 the author enlarges R_{m-1} with arbitrary vertices of W_{m-1} to reach size n/2 and then asserts at 0062-0063 that S still has 'no neighbor in W_m' because S contains R_{m-1}. This is backwards -- N is monotone upward, so a superset of R_{m-1} has at least as many neighbors, and the added vertices of W_{m-1} \ R_{m-1} are precisely the ones for which nothing is known; they may well be adjacent to W_m. Hence N(S) subset of V \ W_m (line 0065) and the bound |N(S)| <= alpha n (line 0067) are unjustified in this case, and the claimed contradiction collapses. The gap is not repairable by a local fix in the given text; the standard correct argument instead proves |R_i| >= n/2 for every i by induction (|N(R_{i-1})| >= n/2 + alpha n and |W_i| >= (1-alpha)n force |N(R_{i-1}) cap W_i| >= n/2), so the small case never arises. Since the second case is a genuine possibility that the proof must cover, the argument as written is invalid.
